stem: Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards side of lesion
Contralateral weakness of the face and arm
fact: Loss of two-point discrimination localizes more strongly to parietal sensory cortex than to the frontal lobe.
mnemonic: Frontal moves and plans; parietal discriminates touch.
finding: Two-point discrimination is a parietal cortical sensory function; the other listed features can arise from frontal regions.

stem: Regarding cerebrospinal fluid, which of the following statements is NOT correct:
options: The total volume of CSF is around 130 mL.
The bulk of CSF formation occurs in the lateral ventricles.
The inferior horn of the lateral ventricle projects into the temporal lobe.
The lateral ventricles are connected to the third ventricle by the cerebral aqueduct.
The fourth ventricle lies within the brainstem.
fact: The lateral ventricles connect to the third ventricle through the interventricular foramina of Monro; the cerebral aqueduct connects the third and fourth ventricles.
mnemonic: Monro joins lateral to third; aqueduct joins third to fourth.
finding: The ventricular-system reference distinguishes the foramina of Monro from the cerebral aqueduct and supports the displayed incorrect statement.

stem: The vertebral artery is a branch of which of the following blood vessels:
fact: Each vertebral artery arises from the corresponding subclavian artery.
finding: The vertebral-artery reference identifies the subclavian artery as its origin.

stem: The internal capsule primarily contains which types of white matter fibres:
fact: The internal capsule is a compact collection of projection fibres linking the cerebral cortex with subcortical structures, brainstem, and spinal cord.
mnemonic: Internal capsule projects cortex to below.
finding: The internal-capsule reference supports projection fibres as the primary fibre type.

stem: Damage to Broca's area will most likely result in which of the following clinical features:
fact: Damage to Broca area in the dominant inferior frontal region causes expressive dysphasia.
mnemonic: Broca builds speech, so damage blocks expression.
finding: The Broca-area reference supports dominant frontal expressive-language localization.

stem: Which of the following brainstem nuclei is NOT located in the pons:
fact: The trochlear nucleus lies in the midbrain; facial, abducens, trigeminal, and vestibulocochlear nuclei are associated with the pons.
mnemonic: Pons hosts V, VI, VII, VIII; IV is midbrain.
finding: The brainstem reference supports trochlear nucleus as the exception.

stem: A 25 year old woman presents to ED complaining of unsteadiness of her feet and slurred speech. On examination she demonstrates past-pointing, she is unable to perform the heel-shin test and she has nystagmus. The lesion would most likely be in the:
fact: Past-pointing, impaired heel-shin testing, nystagmus, ataxia, and slurred speech are cerebellar signs.
mnemonic: DANISH signs point to the cerebellum.
finding: The cerebellar-dysfunction reference supports the displayed cerebellum localization and DANISH sign list.

stem: What of the following type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the optic radiation in the right parietal lobe:
fact: The upper optic radiations pass through the parietal lobe and carry the contralateral lower visual field; a right parietal lesion causes left inferior quadrantanopia.
mnemonic: Parietal carries the lower field; right side loses left lower quadrant.
finding: The visual-field reference supports left inferior quadrantanopia from right parietal optic-radiation involvement.

stem: A 40 year old female presents to ED complaining of complete visual loss in her right eye. On fundoscopy you note a pale retina and a cherry red spot. You suspect an emboli. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely the source of the emboli:
fact: The ophthalmic artery arises from the internal carotid artery and gives rise to the central retinal artery, an end artery whose occlusion can cause monocular blindness with a cherry-red spot.
mnemonic: ICA gives ophthalmic, then central retinal artery.
sourceLabel: NCBI Bookshelf central retinal artery occlusion
finding: The retinal-artery reference supports internal carotid origin of the embolic pathway.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the parietal optic radiation:
fact: A parietal optic-radiation lesion affects fibres carrying the contralateral lower visual field and causes contralateral inferior quadrantanopia.
mnemonic: Parietal radiations carry the lower quadrant.
finding: The visual-field reference supports contralateral inferior quadrantanopia from parietal optic-radiation involvement.
